decisions.reason: As a related extension of the core wafer business that remained visible beyond launch, it is likely close enough to aspiration levels for management to keep it while using existing process know-how and available slack.

This product fits the firm's established thin-wafer handling offer and customer base very closely, so a behavioral-theory management would be inclined to retain it unless results clearly fell below aspiration.
Because it was presented as a flagship and aligns with the firm's direction toward more complex packaging wafers, management is likely to tolerate some uncertainty and keep it despite moderate risk.
The off-the-shelf wafer brand is highly consistent with the firm's core capabilities, narrow product domain, and stated strategic focus, making it the least likely candidate for withdrawal.

Being more distant from the established business, this product is the most likely to fall short of aspiration and prompt problemistic search that reallocates resources back to stronger core and development projects.
